title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X is a variety over a field K, with Γ = Gal(K̄/K). Π̂_1(X) is the profinite étale fundamental groupoid, and Γ acts on it when the base points are K-rational. Earlier pages derived formulas (6), (10) and (11) for how Γ acts on composites of paths and for the left/right translation formulas. This page writes down the obvious action axiom (28), ^{uv}l = ^u(^v l), for u, v in Γ and a path l : x → y.

For rational x, y, the path ^u l is again a path x → y. Since Π(x,y) is a left torsor under π_1(X,y) and a right torsor under π_1(X,x), one can write ^u l = g_l(u)·l = l·f_l(u). Concretely, g_l(u) = ^u l·l^{-1} lies in π̂_1(X,y), and f_l(u) = l^{-1}·^u l lies in π̂_1(X,x).

Applying (6), the compatibility of the action with composition, gives:
- (29) g_l(uv) = ^u g_l(v)·g_l(u), equivalently g_l^{-1}(uv) = g_l^{-1}(u)·^u g_l^{-1}(v);
- (30) f_l(uv) = f_l(u)·^u f_l(v).

So f_l and g_l^{-1} are ordinary (crossed-homomorphism) 1-cocycles of Γ with values in π̂_1(X,x) and π̂_1(X,y) respectively. Grothendieck calls f a 'right' cocycle and g a 'left' cocycle, and they are related through the isomorphism π_1(l). He notes that the f-formula looks nicer here, whereas for (10)–(11) the g-formula did. These cocycles are exactly the cocycles of the Γ-torsor of étale paths Π̂_1(X)(x,y), right under π̂_1(X,x) and left under π̂_1(X,y), with l serving as an origin.

A marginal note asks for an explicit description of the 'bicocycles' (f_l, g_l) attached to Γ-bitorsors under (π̂_1(X,y), π̂_1(X,x)).

The next page shows that changing l changes the cocycles by coboundaries. This yields classes in H^1(Γ, π̂_1(X,x)) and H^1(Γ, π̂_1(X,y)) attached to a pair of rational points: a two-point non-abelian Kummer / period map, which is the basic set-up behind the section conjecture.
errors: Minor imprecision: from the definitions, g_l(u) = l·f_l(u)·l^{-1}. So the isomorphism π_1(l): a ↦ l a l^{-1} carries f_l to g_l, not to g_l^{-1} as the text suggests. Moreover, π_1(l) is not Γ-equivariant: it intertwines the two actions only up to the inner automorphism by g_l(u). So 'déduits l'un de l'autre' holds only in this twisted sense.
The formulas require x, y to be K-rational (so that ^u l is again a path x → y). This page leaves that implicit; the margin of the next page makes it explicit.

ideas.what: Galois cocycle attached to an étale path between rational points: u ↦ l^{-1}·^u l, with the path set as a Γ-equivariant torsor/bitorsor
ideas.modern_name: Non-abelian Kummer map / class of the path torsor in H^1(G_K, π_1(X,x)); étale path torsors
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Grothendieck's 1983 letter to Faltings (section conjecture); systematized by Deligne (1989, P^1 minus three points) and used by Kim (2005, non-abelian Chabauty)
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983), map from rational points to sections / H^1; SGA1 for the groupoid and torsor formalism

ideas.what: Left/right cocycle conventions for a bitorsor and their exchange via conjugation by a path
ideas.modern_name: Bitorsors and their cocycle description (non-abelian cohomology)
ideas.where_published: Bitorsor language appears in SGA 7 (Exp. VII, Grothendieck) and in Giraud

ideas.what: Marginal wish to describe explicitly the 'bicocycles' (f_l, g_l) classifying Γ-bitorsors
ideas.modern_name: Non-abelian H^1 with values in a crossed module / bitorsor classification

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine cocycle computations defining the Galois cocycle of the étale path torsor between rational points. The construction is standard and known through Grothendieck's 1983 letter to Faltings, Deligne 1989 and Kim. Its only interest is as an early (post-1978) written form of the two-point Kummer map in Grothendieck's own hand.
transcription_corrections: First line likely reads 'essentiellement triviale, qui fait pendant à (6)' rather than 'essentielle trivial'.

The final line should probably read 'qui bien sûr n'est autre que Π̂_1(X)(x,y)', i.e. the set of paths from x to y in the fundamental groupoid. This matches the next page's statement that ℓ plays the role of an 'élément origine'.
In the margin, 'de Γ dans Γ' is doubtful. The sense is bicocycles of Γ with values in the pair (π̂_1(X,y), π̂_1(X,x)).
In the margin, the hat on Π_1 (Π̂_1) seems intended throughout, matching the body text.
